name: Standing hip extension
summary: Holding a wall, take one straight leg back behind you from the hip without leaning forward.
setup: Stand side-on to the phone, hands on a wall in front, working leg nearest the phone. Keeping the knee straight and the trunk upright, take the leg back 15–25°, squeeze the buttock, return.
brief: Stand with the hands on a wall in front. Keeping the knee straight and the trunk upright, take the working leg back 15 to 25 degrees, squeeze the buttock, then return.
why: The leg swings back in the camera plane, so its angle counts the reps, and the trunk tipping forward to fake the range shows as the shoulder–hip line tilting.
tempo: Back 2 s, squeeze 1 s, return 2 s.
progression: Band around the ankle anchored in front.
contraindications: Lower back pain on the swing.

faults.label: Leaning forward to go further
faults.tip: The range is small on purpose. Leaning forward moves the work to the lower back.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Arching the lower back
faults.tip: Brace lightly so the movement comes from the hip, not from the spine extending.

faults.label: Swinging the leg too far back
faults.tip: Most people only have 10–15° of true hip extension; the rest comes from arching the back.

faults.label: Bending the knee
faults.tip: A bent knee lets the hamstring take the movement instead of the glute.

guide.stop: Back pain, or pinching at the back of the hip.

points.t: Upright and still; the hip moves, the spine does not.
